why.heading: Why Mauritius Is a Top Honeymoon Destination
subheading: Mauritius suits couples who’d rather do very little, very well. The lagoons are the kind of turquoise you only see in photos, the beaches stay quiet, and the resorts treat a honeymoon as the main event. The flight from Malaysia is long at around 8 to 9 hours, but most couples find the privacy is worth it. Couples still choosing between islands often

subheading.text: weigh Mauritius against Bali and Europe

subheading: on cost, flight time and pace.

highlights.title: Choosing the Right Coast
highlights.body: Each side of the island has its own feel, so pick the coast before the resort. The north is lively, the west is calm with the best sunsets, and the east is quiet and secluded. The south is wilder and less developed, which makes it better for a day drive than a base.

highlights.title: What to Look for in a Resort
highlights.body: Look for adults-only sections, beachfront or overwater villas, and half-board or all-inclusive so meals aren’t one more decision. Ask what the resort gives honeymooners for free, because upgrades and a private dinner are common.

highlights.title: Island Life and Practical Tips
highlights.body: Mauritius is small, so even a quiet resort has day trips within easy reach, and English and French are both widely spoken. The local food is worth leaving the resort for, and Malaysian passport holders can currently visit visa-free for up to 90 days.

zones.heading: Where to Stay and Why
zones.subheading: Pick the coast that matches the honeymoon you have in mind. These are the three most couples choose between.

areas.name: North Coast
areas.description: The most developed resort area, with restaurants and some nightlife close by. It’s a good pick if you want relaxation with a bit of evening buzz.

areas.name: West Coast
areas.description: Calmer water, dramatic sunsets and plenty of water sports and excursions close by.

areas.name: East Coast
areas.description: The quietest and most private resorts on the island. It’s best for couples who care more about tranquillity than things to do.

bestTime.heading: Best Time to Visit Mauritius
bestTime.body: Mauritius works all year, so it comes down to weather and crowds.

seasons.name: Dry Season
seasons.description: Cooler, less humid and generally the most comfortable time for beach days and sightseeing. The east and south coasts can get windy in July and August.

seasons.name: Warm and Wet
seasons.description: Hotter, more humid and wetter, with warmer sea. Cyclone risk is highest from January to March, although most trips in these months go ahead as planned.

options.label: Resort Stay
options.description: A short but proper honeymoon, mostly beach and spa time with one excursion.

options.label: Resort and Island Tours
options.description: The most common length, with enough time for a resort stay plus Île aux Cerfs, Chamarel and the south coast.

options.label: Two Coasts
options.description: For couples who want to see more of the island, such as a quiet east coast resort for a few nights, then somewhere livelier on the west or north.
